newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-DORTMUND MOVE PAST AUXERRE TO SET UP CLASH WITH UNITED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND MOVE PAST AUXERRE TO SET UP CLASH WITH UNITED.

text.p: Midfielder Lars Ricken fired Borussia Dortmund to a 1-0 win over Auxerre on Wednesday which gave the German club a European Cup semifinal clash against Manchester United.
Borussia, 3-1 up from the first leg of their quarter-final tie, resisted first half pressure before carving out an opening in the 59th minute.

Ricken, set up by a pass from striker Stephane Chapuisat, seized his chance from 25 metres. His shot took a deflection off Auxerre midfielder Philippe Violeau's leg and left French goalkeeper Lionel Charbonnier helpless.
Auxerre dominated the first half but failed to breach the visitors' tight defence, despite the absence of the influential Stefan Reuter, who was sent off in the first leg.
Dortmund keeper Stefan Klos was tested after 11 minutes by a powerful shot from just outside the box by Antoine Sibierski which he punched over the bar.
A header by Bernard Diomede went just wide in the 26th minute.
Dortmund threatened only once in the first half, when Karlheinz Riedle produced a headed effort from a cross by Chapuisat, but Charbonnier was ideally placed.

Once ahead, the Germans took control against tiring opponents, who won their first league title last year and dreamed of emulating Marseille, Monaco, Paris St Germain and Nantes, who all reached the European Cup semifinals in the last four years.
Auxerre also hoped to avenge a defeat on penalties to Dortmund in a UEFA Cup semifinal clash in 1993.
"Our elimination is a logical one, even if we would have deserved at least a draw in the second leg," said Auxerre trainer Guy Roux.
"There are guys in the Dortmund side who have won both the World Cup and the European championships. That's a bit too much for a young team like ours."
Dortmund did just what they had to do to keep alive their chances of becoming the first German club to lift the European Cup since Bayern Munich 21 years ago.

"Our defeat against Stuttgart (in the league on Saturday) probably helped us," said veteran defender Juergen Kohler. "We knew we had to stay focused for 90 minutes to qualify and that's exactly what we did."
For the semifinal first leg, Borussia will be without defender and captain Matthias Sammer, who received his second yellow card in the competition for a foul on Diomede in the 60th minute.
"Our goal is to win the European Cup and I believe we can make it," warned Kohler. "We can't expect easy matches from now on but seriously, I think we can make it."
